headline: Broad egress plus shared API/file surfaces create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; no direct evidence of a hard conflict or compliance breach.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: opik can call REST APIs and has broad network egress, while plano accepts OpenAI-compatible chat completions and reads config.yaml. If opik outputs are fed into plano through a shared workspace or API pipeline, injected instructions in content could be treated as trusted. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF opik outputs are copied into plano prompts or configs without sanitization
IF both agents share a workspace or message channel that carries untrusted text
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiting wrapper around opik outputs
Require plano to ignore instruction-like text in upstream content
Use a separate staging file for any handoff between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every transferred field

B_data_leakage.rationale: opik has broad network egress and plano also has broad egress plus touches logs, traces, metrics, and config.yaml. If they share a workspace or if opik forwards content into plano, sensitive operational data could flow out through either agent. No direct shared-storage evidence is present, so this is an inferred default-path risk rather than a proven leak.
conditions: IF opik and plano share files, prompts, or logs containing sensitive material
IF plano forwards its context or config-derived data to external APIs
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Redact logs and traces before any handoff
Disable transfer of raw file contents between agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but opik only exposes REST API calls and plano does not report filesystem write, subprocess, or multi-instance support. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable write targets, so a direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because the shared API surface could still collide in an orchestrated deployment.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API resource
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable backend without locking
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable endpoints
Serialize writes through one coordinator
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: opik can emit evaluation or observability outputs over REST, and plano consumes OpenAI-compatible chat completions. If plano treats opik-generated text as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into downstream travel-planning responses. There is no documented verification step between them, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF plano uses opik output as prompt context or decision input
IF no verification or human review is inserted between the agents
mitigations: Insert a validation step before plano consumes opik output
Require citations or structured schemas for transferred facts
Flag low-confidence upstream content for review
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source with docs-only evidence and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is stated. opik touches no data classes in the profile, while plano touches logs, traces, and metrics, so a compliance issue is possible only if regulated data is introduced into plano's telemetry path. The pair itself does not prove a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent into plano logs, traces, or metrics
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not documented here
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in telemetry fields
Review retention settings in config.yaml
Document data-class handling for both agents
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
